Now let's consider independent test for duplicate predicates, tautology built from disjunction etc. Could construct small exhaustive enumeration of predicate truth masks abstractly not necessarily semantically realizable, compare `_discover_rules` to brute over masks. We'll test random P up to10, n/u small including arbitrary masks. This validates discovery exactly.

cd /workspace && timeout 180 python3 - <<'PY'
import sys,random,itertools
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/submission')
from netnomos.finite import _discover_rules
rng=random.Random(5)
for it in range(10000):
    P=rng.randint(0,10); n=rng.randint(1,12); u=rng.randint(1,30); w=rng.randint(1,4)
    # arbitrary masks
    T=[rng.getrandbits(n) for _ in range(P)]
    U=[rng.getrandbits(u) for _ in range(P)]
    if P==0:
      # skip because allones(0)=0 could weird no clauses
      exp=[]
    allT=(1<<n)-1;allU=(1<<u)-1
    exp=[]
    for L in range(1,min(w,P)+1):
      for C in itertools.combinations(range(P),L):
        if not all(any((T[p]>>i)&1 for p in C) for i in range(n)):continue
        ws=[]
        for p in C:
          f=next((i for i in range(n) if ((T[p]>>i)&1) and not any(((T[q]>>i)&1) for q in C if q!=p)),None)
          if f is None:break
          ws.append(f)
        else:
          cex=next((i for i in range(u) if not any((U[p]>>i)&1 for p in C)),None)
          if cex is not None:exp.append({'clause':list(C),'witnesses':ws,'counterexample':cex})
    got=_discover_rules(P,w,T,U,n,u)
    if got!=exp:
      print('FAIL',it,P,n,u,w,T,U,exp,got);break
else:print('all arbitrary mask tests pass')
